names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 octombrie.
Read out of saint.gr's list of the twelve on its page for the Synaxis of 30 Ιουνίου, «Ιάκωβος του Αλφαίου», with no rank word attached.
The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 867, headed «Апостол Иаков Алфеев», with the rank word and the patronymic epithet left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. октобар ст. ст., „Св. апостол Јаков.“ — Св. is «saint» and not a rank, and апостол is the `apostle` this corpus puts in `types`, so both come off and the bare personal name is the whole of the form. **The heading gives him no patronymic**, where the Romanian stores «Iacob al lui Alfeu» and the Greek «Ιάκωβος του Αλφαίου», so there is nothing fuller to store from this book. `foldchk.py` measured the string as held by five other folders before this day, all of them `sr`; the six-folder fold is read in the `serbian` row’s note and in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`.

feast.note: His name page lists one other day, «30 июня (12 ап.)», the synaxis of the Twelve Apostles. One row per church is the schema, so the June day is recorded here and he does not render on it — which is also the day saint.gr keeps him on, so the Greek row of this folder and this one are the same man on two different days of two calendars.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 9 октября ст. ст. — «Ап. Иакова Алфеева (I).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the first of the day's two icons, «Совершается служба с полиелеем» — a service with the polyeleos — and it stands immediately before his line and his alone. The second icon, the plain service, stands a few words later, immediately before Andronicus and his wife, which is what makes the first one his rather than the paragraph's.

attestations.note: The Russian dates him «(I)», the first century, where neither folder's other row carries a year; no `dates` are proposed from a bare century for an apostle whose death year neither page gives. Its two lives for him add the brother and the places: Matthew the Evangelist's brother, preaching in Judaea, Edessa, Gaza and Eleutheropolis, and a death by crucifixion at Ostracine in Egypt.

feast.note: Doxologia keeps him twice: its calendar prints him on 9 octombrie and again on 30 iunie — «Soborul Sfinților 12 Apostoli». One attestation row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. The 30 iunie line is the Synaxis of the Twelve, which names each apostle in turn. Read 25 September 2026.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul pe 9 octombrie — «Sfântul Apostol Iacob al lui Alfeu»

feast.note: saint.gr keeps 30 Ιουνίου as the Synaxis of the Twelve Apostles, a common commemoration of all of them, and its page names each apostle in turn, this one among them. His own Greek day has not been read in this wave, and saint.gr will have a page for it; the corpus keeps one feast to a church, so the synaxis day is what is recorded here and whether the proper day should replace it is a question left to the writer (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 30ης Ιουνίου — «Σύναξη των Αγίων Δώδεκα Αποστόλων», whose page names him among the twelve
Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.10.2026 (9. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. апостол Јаков.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted whole, **with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints**, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN §4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because `srbody.mjs` and `sr-cand.mjs` both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends `. ` in the source. **An earlier wave of this reading quoted off the stripped output and wrote into its notes that the headings carry no closing stop, which the raw page contradicts for its own days as well as for these** — the rows of that wave are outside this reader’s range and are a finding for the author, not something fixed here. **A READER WHO FINDS ALMOST NOTHING NEW SHOULD SAY SO, AND THIS IS THAT ENTRY.** Everything it tells is already on this folder from the Romanian, the Greek synaxis page and the two Russian lives: the son of Alphaeus, one of the twelve great apostles, own brother of the apostle and evangelist Matthew, witness of the Lord’s words and wonders; the preaching allotted to him at Eleutheropolis and the places round it after Pentecost, and then in Egypt; the casting out of demons and the healing of every sickness in the name of the Lord Jesus; and the crucifixion at Ostracine. TWO SMALL ADDITIONS AND ONE SPECIFICATION. The entry names the fruit of the preaching in institutional terms the other books do not — churches were founded and set in order, priests and bishops appointed — and it adds the Lord’s **passion, resurrection and ascension** to the list of what he witnessed. It also says who crucified him: од незнабожаца, by the heathen, where the Russian life says only that he was crucified. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND NECESSARILY SO: the folder holds `dates: null` and **this entry prints no year for anything**. The appended paragraph carries no four-digit year at all, deliberately — with neither a birth nor a death on the folder, `date-audit`’s `stated` reads its prose for both. Measured after the write: `stated` unmoved. `types` UNTOUCHED at `apostle`, corroborated by апостол and by «један од дванаест великих апостола». `related` UNTOUCHED: `matthew-the-apostle` is already there and the brotherhood this entry asserts is exactly the row that holds it; `andrew-the-first-called` is already there from the Russian life and this entry does not name him. No `locations`, no `office`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE FOLD, AND IT GOES FROM FIVE FOLDERS TO SIX. `foldchk.py` measured «Јаков» before this day as held by five folders, all of them `sr` and all from earlier Serbian waves: `james-of-nisibis`, `james-of-samosata`, `james-of-studion`, `james-son-of-zebedee` and `james-the-confessor`. **The gate has been printing that five-folder row as unread, because no key was ever added for it**; the key for the six is written into `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in the same commit, which is the second of the two acts that reading a fold is. Six men on six days: the bishop of Nisibis on 13 January, the martyr of Samosata on 29 January, the confessor of Studion on 24 March, the confessor bishop on 21 March, the apostle son of Zebedee on 30 April, and this apostle son of Alphaeus on 9 October. The bare Serbian forename is the whole of what they share. TWO OF THE DAY’S FIVE ENTRIES ARE REFUSED UNDER RULING 3 and are named here so that the next reader does not have to find them again. «Св. Димитрије патријарх Александријски», the eleventh bishop of Alexandria after Mark the Evangelist, who governed from 189 to 231 and in whose time Pantaenus of the catechetical school was sent to India and found there the Gospel Matthew had written in Hebrew: **forty-six folders are displayed as a Demetrius and not one of them is of Alexandria.** «Св. Стеван деспот српски», son of the despot Djuradj and Jerina, blinded at Adrianople with his brother Grgur, despot of Serbia from 1458, married to Angelina the daughter of Skanderbeg, dead in Italy in 1468 and lying at Krušedol: **fifty-four folders are displayed as a Stephen and not one of them is this despot, nor does the corpus hold Angelina, Grgur, Mara or the son Maximus named in the entry.** A person the Prologue names but no folder holds gets no folder from a reader, so both are a reading for the report and neither is in any prose.

hymns.text: Apostole Sfinte Iacob, roagă pe Milostivul Dumnezeu, ca să dăruiască iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Apostol Iacob al lui Alfeu

english.text: Holy Apostle James, entreat the merciful God to grant our souls forgiveness of our sins.

hymns.text: Οἱ τῶν Ἀποστόλων πρωτόθρονοι, καὶ τῆς Οἰκουμένης διδάσκαλοι, τῷ Δεσπότῃ τῶν ὅλων πρεσβεύσατε, εἰρήνην τῆ οἰκουμένῃ δωρήσασθαι, καὶ ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, on the page of «Σύναξη των Αγίων Δώδεκα Αποστόλων»

english.text: First-enthroned of the Apostles and teachers of the whole world, intercede with the Master of all things that He grant peace to the world and great mercy to our souls.

hymns.text: Ἀπόστολοι Ἅγιοι, πρεσβεύσατε τῷ ἐλεήμονι Θεῷ , ἵνα πταισμάτων ἄφεσιν, παράσχῃ ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ´ — the common of the apostles, naming nobody, on the page of «Σύναξη των Αγίων Δώδεκα Αποστόλων»

english.text: Holy Apostles, intercede with the merciful God, that He grant to our souls the forgiveness of our offences.

hymns.text: Τοὺς ἀσφαλεῖς καὶ θεοφθόγγους κήρυκας, τὴν κορυφὴν τῶν Μαθητῶν σου Κύριε, προσελάβου εἰς ἀπόλαυσιν, τῶν ἀγαθῶν σου καὶ ἀνάπαυσιν, τοὺς πόνους γὰρ ἐκείνων καὶ τὸν θάνατον, ἐδέξω ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ὁλοκάρπωσιν, ὁ μόνος γινώσκων τὰ ἐγκάρδια.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τοὺς ἀσφαλεῖς, on the page of «Σύναξη των Αγίων Δώδεκα Αποστόλων»

english.text: The sure and God-inspired heralds, the chief of Thy disciples, Thou hast taken to Thyself, O Lord, into the enjoyment of Thy good things and into rest; for Thou didst accept their labours and their death above every whole burnt offering, O Thou who alone knowest the secrets of the heart.
